title: Session fixation and logging out
summary: Issue a fresh session id at login, and make logout actually end the session on the server.

steps.title: Session fixation
body: Many sites give anonymous visitors a session (for a basket, a language choice). Now imagine login simply *marks that existing session* as logged in:
1. Mallory visits the site and gets  sid=AAA  (anonymous).
2. She gets Ada's browser to use sid=AAA:
a link with ?sid=AAA on a site that accepts ids from the URL,
or a cookie set by a compromised subdomain.
3. Ada logs in. The server marks session AAA as "ada".
4. Mallory, who knows AAA, is now logged in as Ada.
That is **session fixation**: the attacker doesn't steal the id, they *choose* it in advance. The fix is simple and absolute:
- **Issue a brand-new session id whenever the privilege level changes**: at login, at logout, when stepping up to MFA or an admin role. Delete the old one.
- Never accept an id the server didn't issue (and never take ids from URLs).

steps.prompt: Which login handler is safe from session fixation?
options: Verify the password, delete the session id the request came with, create a new random id for the user, set it in the cookie
Verify the password, then store the username in the session the request came with
Verify the password, then set the cookie to the same id with a longer Max-Age
Verify the password, then hash the existing session id and use the hash as the new id
steps.explain: Any id the attacker knew before login must be worthless after it. A hash of a known id is just as known to the attacker, who can compute it too.

steps.prompt: This simulates a store that upgrades the old id instead of rotating it. What does it print?
code: var sessions = new Dictionary<string, string> { ["AAA"] = "" };   // Mallory's anonymous id
// Ada's browser was tricked into using AAA, and she logs in:
// Mallory sends a request with the id she planted:
steps.explain: Because the id survived the login, the attacker who planted it shares the authenticated session.

steps.title: Logging out properly
body: A logout button that only clears the cookie in the browser does not log anyone out. A copy of the id (stolen earlier, or in another tab) still works until the session times out. Logout has two halves:
1. **On the server: delete the session.** This is the part that matters. Once the record is gone, the id is worthless everywhere.

2. **In the browser: expire the cookie.** `ctx.Response.Cookies.Delete("sid")` sends `Set-Cookie: sid=; expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT; path=/`. A `Clear-Site-Data: "cookies"` header goes further.
Also offer **"log out everywhere"** (delete every session for the user) and do it automatically when the password changes or an account is recovered.
Respond `204 No Content`. Use `POST` for logout, not `GET`, so a link or image on another site can't log your users out.

steps.prompt: Which half of logout is each one?
items: Remove the session record from the store
Delete every session of the user after a password change
steps.explain: Only the server-side steps make a stolen id stop working. The browser steps are good manners.

steps.prompt: Arrange the body of a fixation-proof login handler.
lines: if (ctx.Request.Cookies["sid"] is string old) sessions.TryRemove(old, out _);
also: if (ctx.Request.Cookies["sid"] is string old) sessions.TryRemove(old, out _);
if (ctx.Request.Cookies["sid"] is string old) sessions.TryRemove(old, out _);
if (ctx.Request.Cookies["sid"] is string old) sessions.TryRemove(old, out _);
steps.explain: Check the password first. The new id must be created before it is stored and set in the cookie, and the old id must be removed before the response is returned.

steps.prompt: After `POST /logout`, the server answers `204` and expires the cookie, but forgets to delete the session record. What can an attacker who copied the session id yesterday do?
options: Keep using it until the session times out
Only read data, not change it
Nothing, as long as the cookie was HttpOnly
steps.explain: The attacker sends the id in their own `Cookie` header. The browser's copy is irrelevant; only deleting the server-side record revokes it.

steps.title: Rotate on login, revoke on logout
prompt: The starter works but has a fixation bug: `POST /login` reuses whatever `sid` the browser sent. Users are ada / `correct horse` and grace / `hopper-1906`. **Run checks** starts the server and calls it.
1. Fix `POST /login`: on success, **remove** the session the request came with (if any) and issue a **new** id.
2. Fix `GET /visit` so it only keeps an incoming `sid` that the server actually issued (one that is in `sessions`); otherwise it makes a new one.
3. Add `POST /logout`: remove the session from `sessions`, expire the cookie with `ctx.Response.Cookies.Delete("sid", ...)`, and answer `204`. Logging out without a session is also `204`.
`GET /me` must then answer `401` for the old ids.
starter: // Demo users. Passwords are stored as PBKDF2 hashes, never as text.
var sessions = new ConcurrentDictionary<string, string>();   // session id -> username
HttpOnly = true, Secure = true, SameSite = SameSiteMode.Lax, Path = "/",
if (id is null || !sessions.TryGetValue(id, out var user)) return Results.Unauthorized();
// An anonymous visitor gets a session too (think: a shopping basket).
return Results.Json(new { error = "Invalid username or password." }, statusCode: 401);
// BUG: logging in upgrades whatever session id the browser already had.
// Unknown users still pay for one hash, so timing doesn't reveal which names exist.
solution: // Demo users. Passwords are stored as PBKDF2 hashes, never as text.
var sessions = new ConcurrentDictionary<string, string>();   // session id -> username
HttpOnly = true, Secure = true, SameSite = SameSiteMode.Lax, Path = "/",
if (id is null || !sessions.TryGetValue(id, out var user)) return Results.Unauthorized();
// An anonymous visitor gets a session too (think: a shopping basket).
var id = existing is not null && sessions.ContainsKey(existing)
return Results.Json(new { error = "Invalid username or password." }, statusCode: 401);
if (ctx.Request.Cookies["sid"] is string old) sessions.TryRemove(old, out _);
if (ctx.Request.Cookies["sid"] is string id) sessions.TryRemove(id, out _);
ctx.Response.Cookies.Delete("sid", new CookieOptions { Path = "/", Secure = true, HttpOnly = true, SameSite = SameSiteMode.Lax });
// Unknown users still pay for one hash, so timing doesn't reveal which names exist.
hints: In `/login`: `if (ctx.Request.Cookies["sid"] is string old) sessions.TryRemove(old, out _);` then always make a new id.
In `/visit`: keep the incoming id only when `sessions.ContainsKey(existing)`.

static class DojoTests
public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
var c = NewClient(http);
await Dojo.TryAsync("Fixation could be checked", async () =>
var visit = await Send(c, HttpMethod.Get, "/visit", null);
var planted = ValueOf(SetCookie(visit, "sid"));
Dojo.Check("GET /visit hands out a sid", planted is not null, "no sid cookie");
var fresh = await Login(c, "ada", "correct horse", planted);
Dojo.Check("login issues a new sid", fresh is not null && fresh != planted, "the id after login was " + (fresh ?? "missing"));
DojoWeb.Status("the planted id is not logged in", 401, await Send(c, HttpMethod.Get, "/me", planted));
Dojo.Eq("the new id is ada", "ada", DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(await Send(c, HttpMethod.Get, "/me", fresh)), "user"));
var chosen = ValueOf(SetCookie(await Send(c, HttpMethod.Get, "/visit", "ATTACKER-CHOSEN"), "sid"));
Dojo.Check("GET /visit doesn't adopt an id it never issued", chosen != "ATTACKER-CHOSEN", "it kept ATTACKER-CHOSEN");
var second = await Login(c, "grace", "hopper-1906", fresh);
DojoWeb.Status("logging in again retires the previous id", 401, await Send(c, HttpMethod.Get, "/me", fresh));
Dojo.Eq("and the newest id works", "grace", DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(await Send(c, HttpMethod.Get, "/me", second)), "user"));
await Dojo.TryAsync("Logout could be checked", async () =>
var sid = await Login(c, "ada", "correct horse");
var copy = sid;   // an attacker's copy of the same id
var r = await Send(c, HttpMethod.Post, "/logout", sid);
DojoWeb.Status("POST /logout gets 204", 204, r);
var cleared = SetCookie(r, "sid");

Dojo.Check("logout expires the sid cookie", cleared is not null && (cleared.Contains("1970") || cleared.Contains("max-age=0", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)), cleared ?? "no Set-Cookie: sid=...");
DojoWeb.Status("a copy of the old id no longer works", 401, await Send(c, HttpMethod.Get, "/me", copy));
DojoWeb.Status("POST /logout without a session also gets 204", 204, await Send(c, HttpMethod.Post, "/logout", null));
static HttpClient NewClient(HttpClient http) =>
new(new HttpClientHandler { UseCookies = false, AllowAutoRedirect = false }) { BaseAddress = http.BaseAddress };
static string? SetCookie(HttpResponseMessage r, string name) =>
r.Headers.TryGetValues("Set-Cookie", out var values) ? values.FirstOrDefault(c => c.StartsWith(name + "=")) : null;
static string? ValueOf(string? header) =>
header is null ? null : header.Split(';')[0].Split('=', 2)[1];
static bool HasAttr(string? header, string attr) =>
header is not null && header.Split(';').Skip(1).Select(p => p.Trim())
.Any(p => p.Equals(attr, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) || p.StartsWith(attr + "=", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
static string? Attr(string? header, string attr) =>
header?.Split(';').Skip(1).Select(p => p.Trim())
.FirstOrDefault(p => p.StartsWith(attr + "=", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))?.Split('=', 2)[1];
static Task<HttpResponseMessage> Send(HttpClient c, HttpMethod method, string url, string? sid, object? body = null, string? csrf = null)
var msg = new HttpRequestMessage(method, url);
if (sid is not null) msg.Headers.Add("Cookie", "sid=" + sid);
if (csrf is not null) msg.Headers.Add("X-CSRF-Token", csrf);
if (body is not null) msg.Content = JsonContent.Create(body);
return c.SendAsync(msg);
static async Task<string?> Login(HttpClient c, string user, string password, string? oldSid = null)
var r = await Send(c, HttpMethod.Post, "/login", oldSid, new { username = user, password });
return ValueOf(SetCookie(r, "sid"));
